_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Namibia covering San rock art (Twyfelfontein), Bantu migration, Herero/Nama peoples, German South-West Africa, Herero/Nama genocide (1904–1908, first genocide of the 20th century), South African mandate, SWAPO liberation struggle, independence 1990 (last African colony), and Skeleton Coast.

910.name: San Rock Art and Early Inhabitants
910.description: San hunter-gatherers inhabit Namibia for tens of thousands of years; Twyfelfontein rock engravings are a UNESCO World Heritage site; Damara and Nama Khoikhoi peoples also ancient inhabitants.

sub_clusters.name: Twyfelfontein Rock Engravings
sub_clusters.description: UNESCO World Heritage site in Kunene region with over 2,500 rock engravings and paintings; depict animals, human footprints, and geometric designs; created by San hunter-gatherers.

sub_clusters.name: San and Damara Ancient Populations
sub_clusters.description: San (Bushmen) hunter-gatherers are the earliest inhabitants; Damara people (Khoikhoi linguistic group) establish pastoral communities; diverse ecological adaptations across desert, savanna, and coastal environments.

920.name: Bantu Migration and Pastoral Peoples
920.description: Bantu-speaking peoples migrate into northern and central Namibia; Herero pastoralists and Ovambo agro-pastoralists establish distinct societies.

sub_clusters.name: Ovambo Settlement in Northern Namibia
sub_clusters.description: Ovambo-speaking peoples settle in the well-watered Cuvelai drainage system (Owamboland); develop mixed farming economy; become the largest ethnic group in Namibia.

sub_clusters.name: Herero Migration into Central Namibia
sub_clusters.description: Herero pastoralists migrate from East Africa via the Kaokoveld into central Namibia; cattle-centred culture; holy fire (okuruwo) ritual traditions; competition with Nama for grazing.

930.name: Nama-Herero Conflicts and European Contact
930.description: Nama-Herero wars over cattle and grazing; Oorlam groups introduce firearms; European missionaries and traders arrive; Jonker Afrikaner's dominance.

sub_clusters.name: Nama-Herero Wars and Oorlam Impact
sub_clusters.description: Nama clans clash with Herero over central highlands grazing; Oorlam Afrikaners (Jonker Afrikaner) dominate from Windhoek with firearms and horse tactics.

sub_clusters.name: Maharero's Herero Consolidation
sub_clusters.description: Maharero unites Herero groups; negotiates with German traders and missionaries; Battle of Otjimbingwe 1880; fragile peace between Herero and Nama before German colonisation.

sub_clusters.name: Skeleton Coast and European Maritime Contact
sub_clusters.description: Portuguese navigator Diogo Cão reaches Cape Cross 1486; treacherous Skeleton Coast (shipwrecks, fog, desert); whaling and guano stations; Walvis Bay claimed by Britain 1878.

940.name: German South-West Africa
940.description: Germany colonises Namibia as South-West Africa; land confiscation and cattle seizure provoke the Herero and Nama uprisings; the resulting genocide is the first of the 20th century.

sub_clusters.name: German Colonisation and Land Seizure
sub_clusters.description: Heinrich Göring (father of Hermann) as imperial commissioner; Schutztruppe garrisons; treaties of protection then systematic land and cattle confiscation from Herero and Nama peoples.

sub_clusters.name: Herero and Nama Genocide (1904–1908)
sub_clusters.description: Herero revolt January 1904 under Samuel Maharero; Battle of Waterberg August 1904; General Lothar von Trotha's extermination order (Vernichtungsbefehl); Herero driven into Omaheke Desert; Nama uprising under Hendrik Witbooi; concentration camps (Shark Island); ~65,000 Herero (80%) and ~10,000 Nama (50%) killed. Recognised as the first genocide of the 20th century.

sub_clusters.name: German South-West Africa: Final Years
sub_clusters.description: Diamond rush at Lüderitz 1908; settler colonialism intensifies; World War I — South African forces invade and Germany surrenders South-West Africa in 1915.

940.name: South African Mandate and Apartheid Rule
940.description: South Africa administers Namibia under League of Nations mandate; extends apartheid system; reserves (bantustans) created; resistance grows.

sub_clusters.name: League of Nations Mandate
sub_clusters.description: South Africa receives Class C mandate; treats territory as de facto fifth province; white settlement encouraged; contract labour system for Ovambo workers.

sub_clusters.name: Apartheid Extended to Namibia
sub_clusters.description: South Africa extends apartheid laws; Odendaal Commission (1964) creates bantustans; forced removals; pass laws; Old Location shooting in Windhoek 1959.

950.name: SWAPO Liberation Struggle
950.description: SWAPO leads armed liberation struggle against South African occupation; international legal battles at ICJ; UN recognises Namibian independence right; Border War/Bush War.

sub_clusters.name: SWAPO Formation and Early Resistance
sub_clusters.description: South West Africa People's Organisation (SWAPO) founded 1960 by Sam Nujoma and others; ICJ rules on South Africa's obligations; UN revokes mandate 1966.

sub_clusters.name: Armed Struggle and Border War
sub_clusters.description: PLAN (People's Liberation Army of Namibia) launches armed struggle at Omgulumbashe 26 August 1966; South African Border War/Bush War; Angolan theatre; Cassinga massacre 1978.

sub_clusters.name: UN Resolution 435 and Independence Process
sub_clusters.description: UN Security Council Resolution 435 (1978) mandates supervised elections; linked to Cuban troop withdrawal from Angola; Battle of Cuito Cuanavale 1988 breaks stalemate; elections November 1989; independence 21 March 1990.

960.name: Independent Namibia
960.description: Namibia becomes the last African colony to gain independence; SWAPO dominates politics; reconciliation policy; land reform debates; Germany acknowledges genocide.

sub_clusters.name: Sam Nujoma's Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Nujoma serves three terms; policy of national reconciliation; progressive constitution; Caprivi secessionist attempt 1999; land redistribution begins slowly.

sub_clusters.name: Pohamba and Geingob Presidencies
sub_clusters.description: Hifikepunye Pohamba (2005–2015) wins Mo Ibrahim Prize; Hage Geingob (2015–2024) faces corruption allegations; SWAPO dominance slowly erodes; youth unemployment crisis.

sub_clusters.name: German Genocide Recognition
sub_clusters.description: Germany formally acknowledges Herero and Nama genocide in 2021; €1.1 billion development aid offer; Herero and Nama representatives reject terms as inadequate; reparations debate continues.

sub_clusters.name: Land Reform and Economic Challenges
sub_clusters.description: Willing-seller-willing-buyer land reform; white farmers still own disproportionate land; uranium and diamond mining; conservation economy (communal conservancies); Nana Mbumba becomes first female president 2024.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
